claim: Counterflow Flight A (labeled engineering artifact): an N=3 counterflow ladder (partial-SWAP contacts, MCM-reset advection) on IBM hardware produces a temperature crossing (cold-exit p1 > hot-exit p1, eps_cf > 1/2) that a co-flow control (identical gates, co-current pairing) does not, with an equal-stream null arm bounding readout bias. Engineering demonstration, NOT a quantum-vs-classical advantage claim.

_billing_values.unit: excited-state population p1 = P(measure 1) on the exit qubit, ONE readout-mitigated estimator applied identically to all three arms; in the symmetric-exit instrument (Amendment 5) the estimator is the mean of two versions (direct + terminal-exit-swapped) of that SAME population measurement — a symmetric (order-independent) average, still one currency for every arm
_billing_values.stopping_rule: fixed 10,000 shots per circuit; each arm = 2 circuits (direct + swapped) so 20,000 shots per arm, all frozen in the prereg before submit; identical for all three arms
_billing_values.rejected_convention: no cross-unit conversion arises: all arms are population measurements on the same layout with the same shot count; a per-shot vs per-parcel distinction does not change the unit
_billing_values.baseline_note: the 'baseline' is the CO-FLOW control, EXECUTED on the same hardware in the same job (not simulated); it is not a classical-vs-quantum baseline because no quantum advantage is claimed. The effect is classically expected; the artifact is labeled engineering (Exp139b precedent).

advantage_claimed: none — engineering artifact; the crossing is a classically-expected heat-exchanger effect realized on quantum carriers, graded by survival against the co-flow and null controls
_index_space_check: Mechanical check run: the three arms are NAMED keys (counterflow/co-flow/null), not positionally enumerated; the graded observable crossing=p1(cold_exit)-p1(hot_exit) is fixed arithmetic on two NAMED exit qubits with NO argmin/argmax/first-match/scan-order tie-break. Permuting the arm dict or the result keys does not move any graded number. The only scan-order construct is 'least-busy backend' at SUBMIT, which is (a) not part of the graded result and (b) removed: the flight script PINS the backend by name (frozen in the prereg), so there is no enumeration-order dependence anywhere in the pipeline. Both keys 'no'.
